## §2.1.1: The Quest for Universality & The Syntrix Triad {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-d">STRATUM D: HISTORICAL EXEGESIS (SM, PP. 24–27, EQ. 5)</div>

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
### From Variant Functors ($\mathfrak{F}$) to *Kategorien* ($\mathfrak{K}$)
* Chapter 1 showed how local perspectives glue via sheaf descent, but a sheaf is **passive**: it possesses no internal generative grammar to synthesize higher-rank structures.
* Following **Ernst Cassirer (1910)** (*Substanzbegriff und Funktionsbegriff*), the **Syntrix ($\syntrix$)** dissolves static substantial "things" into a recursive **functorial operand**.

::: {.thm-box}
**The Syntrix Triad (SM, p. 27, Eq. 5):**
$$
\syntrix \equiv \langle \synkolator,\, \metrophor,\, m \rangle \quad \lor \quad \metrophor \equiv (a_i)_n \quad \lor \quad F_1 \equiv \synkolator(a_k)_1^m \quad (1 \le m \le n) \tag{SM-5}
$$

1. **The Metrophor ($\metrophor \equiv (a_i)_n$):** Invariant apodictic base $\mathbf{AP}_0$ (*Idee* $\mathfrak{S}_1$, *Maßträger*).
2. **The Synkolator ($\synkolator$):** Recursive correlation-stage inductor ($F_\gamma \to F_{\gamma+1}$, *Episyllogismus* $k \uparrow$).
3. **The Synkolationsstufe ($m \in \mathbb{N}$):** Operational arity binding $m$ inputs per step.
:::
:::

  <div class="video-caption">Manim Act I: Cassirer Functional Shift &amp; The Syntrix Generative Triad (SM-5)</div>
</div>

::: {.intuition-box .fragment}
**Recursive Unfolding of the Syndrome Tower:**
$$
\metrophor = F_0 \xrightarrow{\;\synkolator_1\;} F_1 \xrightarrow{\;\synkolator_2\;} F_2 \xrightarrow{\;\synkolator_3\;} \cdots \xrightarrow{\;\synkolator_\gamma\;} F_\gamma
$$
Every derived concept traces its semantic warrant back to the unconditioned Metrophor $\metrophor$.
:::
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Chapter 2 transitions from passive observation to active concept generation. To support a Universalquantor U that holds across all observer contexts, the operands cannot be transient propositions; they must be complete hierarchical systems—Kategorien—generated by the Syntrix triad: Metrophor, Synkolator, and Synkolationsstufe.
:::

## §2.1.2–2.1.4: Pyramidal vs. Homogeneous & *Bandsyntrix* {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-d">STRATUM D: SPALTBARKEIT (SM-5a) &amp; BANDSYNTRIX (SM-7)</div>

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
### Two Dependency Architectures
* **Pyramidal Syntrix ($y\syntrix$ — *Diskrete Synkolation*):** Strict level-by-level progression. Syndrome $F_{\gamma+1}$ draws inputs exclusively from the immediately preceding stratum $F_\gamma$.
* **Homogeneous Syntrix ($\homsyntrix$ — *Kontinuierliche Synkolation*):** Cumulative historical memory drawing inputs simultaneously from $\metrophor$ and all preceding layers $(F_1, \dots, F_\gamma)$:
$$
\homsyntrix \equiv \langle\langle \synkolator,\, \metrophor \rangle m \rangle \tag{SM-5a}
$$

::: {.carnap-box .fragment}
**The Principle of *Spaltbarkeit* (SM, p. 29) & *Bandsyntrix* (SM-7):**
1. **Spaltbarkeit:** Every homogeneous Syntrix splits into a purely pyramidal core ($T_{\mathrm{pyr}}$) and a residual historical interaction fragment ($T_{\mathrm{frag}}$).
2. **Existenzbedingung (SM-6) & Bandsyntrix (SM-7):**
$$
\metrophor \equiv (a_i)_n \;\;(n \ge 1), \qquad \metrophor_{\mathrm{band}} \equiv (A_i,\, a_i,\, B_i)_n \tag{SM-6, SM-7}
$$
Discrete syntrices are the degenerate limit $A_i = B_i = a_i$ (**Theorem 2.5**).
:::
:::

</div>

::: {.thm-box .fragment}
**Operational Axes (SM, p. 28):**
* **Metralität:** *Heterometral* (without replacement) vs. *Homometral* (with repetition).
* **Symmetrie:** *Symmetrisch* ($\Sigma_m$-invariant) vs. *Asymmetrisch* (order-sensitive).
:::
:::

## §2.2.1–2.2.2: The $\mathsf{Ban}$-Enriched Colored Operad $\Osyn$ {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATUM A: COMPLETED COLORED BANACH OPERADS (DEFS. 2.2 &amp; 2.3)</div>

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
::: {.intuition-box}
**Why Colored Operads Govern the Syntrix:**
Each hierarchical level $\gamma \in \mathbf{Col} \coloneqq \mathbb{N}_0$ acts as an unforgeable type tag ("color"). An operation $f \in \Osyn(\gamma_1, \dots, \gamma_m; \gamma)$ can fire if and only if its input slots match the exact structural grades of the incoming syndromes.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment}
**Definition 2.2: Completed Free Operad $\widehat{\mathbb{F}}_\pi(E)$ via Colored Trees**
For each non-planar rooted tree $\tau \in \operatorname{Tree}(\vec{\gamma}; \gamma)$, define the vertex tensor space and $\ell^1$-completed free operad:
$$
E(\tau) \coloneqq \widehat{\bigotimes}_{v \in V(\tau)}^\pi E(\operatorname{in}(v); \operatorname{out}(v)), \qquad \widehat{\mathbb{F}}_\pi(E)(\vec{\gamma}; \gamma) \coloneqq \bigoplus_{[\tau] \in \operatorname{Tree}(\vec{\gamma}; \gamma)/\sim}^{\ell^1} E(\tau)_{\Aut(\tau)}
$$
subject to **Operadic Substitution Contraction** ($\|\circ_i\|_{\mathrm{op}} \le 1$) and the **Strict Unit Isometry Axiom** ($\|\operatorname{id}_c\|_{\Osyn(c;c)} = 1$).
:::
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
<div class="video-container">
  <video data-autoplay loop muted playsinline src="media/Ch2_Act3_Colored_Operad_Grafting.mp4"></video>
  <div class="video-caption">Manim Act III (Fig. 2.1): Type-Safe Operadic Tree Grafting $\gamma(f; g, \operatorname{id})$</div>
</div>

::: {.thm-box .fragment}
**Definition 2.3: Syntrix Algebras over $\Osyn$**
An $\Osyn$-algebra on graded Banach spaces $F = \{F_\gamma\}_{\gamma \ge 0}$ is a family of contractive evaluation maps:
$$
\operatorname{ev}_{\vec{\gamma}; \gamma} \colon \Osyn(\gamma_1, \dots, \gamma_m; \gamma) \otpi \big(F_{\gamma_1} \otpi \dots \otpi F_{\gamma_m}\big) \longrightarrow F_\gamma
$$
:::
:::

## §2.2.3: Operational Stabilizers $\Stab(f)$ & Permutohedron $\Pi_3$ {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATUM A: SYMMETRY ORBITS &amp; LAGRANGE INDEX (DEF. 2.4, FIG. 2.2)</div>

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="46%"}
::: {.thm-box}
**Definition 2.4: Profile-Preserving Stabilizers**
For profile $\vec{\gamma} = (\gamma_1, \dots, \gamma_m)$, let $\Sigma_{\vec{\gamma}} \coloneqq \{\sigma \in \Sigma_m \mid \gamma_{\sigma^{-1}(i)} = \gamma_i\}$.

1. **Operational Stabilizer:**
$$
\Stab(f) \;\coloneqq\; \{ \sigma \in \Sigma_{\vec{\gamma}} \mid \sigma \cdot f = f \}
$$
2. **Permutation Asymmetry Measure (Lagrange Index):**
$$
r_f \;\coloneqq\; [\Sigma_{\vec{\gamma}} : \Stab(f)] \;=\; \frac{|\Sigma_{\vec{\gamma}}|}{|\Stab(f)|}
$$
* **Fully Symmetric:** $\Stab(f) = \Sigma_{\vec{\gamma}} \iff r_f = 1$.
* **Completely Asymmetric:** $\Stab(f) = \{e\} \iff r_f = m!$.
:::

## §2.2.4–2.2.5: Free Tree Monad $T_{\mathsf{P}}$ & Bar–Cobar Duality {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATUM A: EPISYLLOGISMUS MONAD &amp; PROSYLLOGISMUS COOPERAD (THM. 2.8)</div>

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.thm-box}
**Definition 2.6: Completed Free Tree Monad $T_{\mathsf{P}}$ (*Episyllogismus* $k \uparrow$)**
For polynomial functor $\mathsf{P}(Y) \coloneqq \bigoplus_{m=1}^M (E(m) \otpi Y^{\otpi m})_{\Sigma_m}$, the $\ell^1$-completed initial algebra of $\mathsf{F}_X(Y) = X \oplus_1 \mathsf{P}(Y)$ is:
$$
T_{\mathsf{P}}(X) \;\cong\; X \oplus_1 \mathsf{P}(T_{\mathsf{P}}(X)) \;\cong\; \bigoplus_{[\tau] \in \mathbf{Tree}/\sim}^{\ell^1} \left( E(\tau) \otpi X^{\otpi \operatorname{Leaves}(\tau)} \right)_{\Aut(\tau)}
$$
Its depth-$K$ truncation $T_{\mathsf{P}}^{(\le K)}$ restricts to $\FinBan \to \FinBan$.
:::

::: {.carnap-box .fragment}
**Definition 2.7 & Theorem 2.8: Bar–Cobar Duality (*Prosyllogismus* $k \downarrow$)**
The downward analytical decomposition of syndromes is governed by the **Prosyllogistic Bar Cooperad** $B(\Osyn) \coloneqq \mathbb{F}^c(s\overline{\Osyn})$ (acting by **tree de-grafting** $\Delta_{\mathrm{prosyl}}$):
$$
\Omega_{\mathrm{cobar}} \;\dashv\; B_{\mathrm{bar}} \;\colon\; \mathbf{dgOp}_{\mathbf{Col}}^{\mathrm{aug}} \;\rightleftarrows\; \mathbf{dgCoop}_{\mathbf{Col}}^{\mathrm{conil}}
$$
The counit $\epsilon_{\mathcal{O}} \colon \Omega_{\mathrm{cobar}}(B_{\mathrm{bar}}(\Osyn)) \xrightarrow{\sim} \Osyn$ is a quasi-isomorphism!
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

  <video data-autoplay loop muted playsinline src="media/Ch2_Act5_Tree_Monad_Bar_Cobar.mp4"></video>
  <div class="video-caption">Manim Act V: Iterative Tree Monad $T_{\mathsf{P}}(X)$ vs. Prosyllogistic Bar Cooperad De-Grafting</div>

::: {.intuition-box .fragment}
**Maurer–Cartan Twisting Morphisms:**
Morphisms $\Omega_{\mathrm{cobar}}(\mathcal{C}) \to \mathcal{O}$ correspond bijectively to degree-$-1$ twisting cochains $\alpha \in \operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ satisfying the Maurer–Cartan equation:
$$
\partial(\alpha) + \alpha \star \alpha = 0
$$
:::
:::

## §2.3–2.4.1: Leveled Category $\mathcal{C}_{\text{SL}}$, Spine & 4 Elementary Structures {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: SHIFT ENDOFUNCTOR &amp; SELECTION REPRESENTATIONS (THM. 2.16)</div>

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
::: {.thm-box}
**Definitions 2.9–2.14: $\mathcal{C}_{\text{SL}}(\mathcal{B})$, $\Shift$ & Spine $\mathcal{C}_{\text{spine}}$**
* Objects $\mathbf{L} = (P_k, S_k, (I_j^+)_{j\ge 1}, O_k)_{k\in\mathbb{N}_0}$ track propositions, stability $S_k$, ancestral parthood $I_k^+$, and Metrophor origin $O_k$.
* The **Level-Shift Functor** $\Shift(\mathbf{L})_k \coloneqq \mathbf{L}_{k+1}$ generates the **thin spine subcategory** $\mathcal{C}_{\text{spine}} \cong (\mathbb{N}_0, \le)$ of shifted free levels $\mathbf{L}^{(k)} \coloneqq \Shift^k(\mathbf{L}^*)$.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment}
**Theorem 2.16: The Selection-Rule Dimension Theorem**
On an $n$-dimensional carrier $V \in \FinBan$ with arity $m$:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\dim \mathcal{S}_{(1)}\text{ (Het, Sym: }\Lambda^m V\text{)} &= \binom{n}{m}, & \dim \mathcal{S}_{(2)}\text{ (Het, Asym: }V^{\underline{\otimes}m}\text{)} &= \frac{n!}{(n-m)!} \\
\dim \mathcal{S}_{(3)}\text{ (Hom, Sym: }\Sym^m V\text{)} &= \binom{n+m-1}{m}, & \dim \mathcal{S}_{(4)}\text{ (Hom, Asym: }V^{\otimes m}\text{)} &= n^m
\end{aligned}
$$
:::
:::

## §2.4.2–2.4.3: *Komplexsynkolatoren* & Dynamical Phase Trichotomy {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: PROGRAMMABLE CLOSURE &amp; ASYMPTOTIC TRICHOTOMY (THM. 2.24)</div>

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
::: {.thm-box}
**Definition 2.22 & Proposition 2.23: *Komplexsynkolatoren* (SM-8)**
Stepping arity $m(\gamma) = \sum_{k=1}^K m_k \mathbf{1}_{I_k}(\gamma)$ across interval partitions $I_k = [\chi(k-1), \chi(k)-1]$:
$$
m_K > \dim\big(F_{\chi(K-1)}\big) \implies \dim \Lambda^{m_K}\big(F_{\chi(K-1)}\big) = \binom{\dim F}{m_K} = 0
$$
forcing deterministic **Syndromabschluß**: $F_\gamma \cong \{0\}$ for all $\gamma \ge \chi(K)$.
:::

::: {.carnap-box .fragment}
**Theorem 2.24: Dynamical Phase Trichotomy of $n_{\gamma+1} = \binom{n_\gamma}{m}$**

1. **Sub-Critical Extinction ($n_0 \le m$):** Terminates in $\le 2$ steps ($n_\gamma = 0\;\forall \gamma \ge 2$).
2. **Critical Equi-Syndromatic Fixed Point ($n_0 = m + 1$):** Strictly constant $n_\gamma = m + 1\;\forall \gamma \ge 0$ (proven in Lean 4: `equisyndromatic_fixed_point`).
3. **Super-Critical Doubly-Exponential ($n_0 \ge m + 2$):**
$$
\lim_{\gamma \to \infty} \frac{1}{m^\gamma} \ln n_\gamma = \theta(n_0, m) > 0, \qquad n_\gamma \sim (m!)^{\frac{1}{m-1}} \exp\!\big(\theta(n_0, m)\, m^\gamma\big)
$$
:::
:::

## §2.5: Boardman–Vogt Tensor & Beck Distributive Law {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: OPERADIC SPALTBARKEIT &amp; MONAD FACTORIZATION (THM. 2.27)</div>

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
::: {.firewall-box}
**Why Naive Free-Tree Substitution Fails I**
On raw unquotiented syntax trees $\mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{pyr}}, \mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{frag}}$, pushing a multi-ary pyramidal node across a fragment node duplicates subtrees, violating Beck's multiplication pentagon.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment}
**Definition 2.26 & Theorem 2.27: Boardman–Vogt Quotient & Beck Law**
Quotienting by the multilinear interchange ideal $\mathcal{I}_{\mathrm{exchange}}$:
$$
\Ohom \;\coloneqq\; \Opyr \otBV \Ofrag \;\coloneqq\; \frac{\Opyr \amalg \Ofrag}{\langle f \circ (g,\dots,g) \sim \sigma_{n,m}\cdot g \circ (f,\dots,f) \rangle}
$$
induces a contractive **Beck Distributive Law** on the $\ell^1$-completed quotient monads:
$$
\widehat{\lambda}_X \colon \overline{T}_{\mathrm{pyr}}\big(\overline{T}_{\mathrm{frag}} X\big) \longrightarrow \overline{T}_{\mathrm{frag}}\big(\overline{T}_{\mathrm{pyr}} X\big), \qquad \|\widehat{\lambda}_X\|_{\mathrm{op}} \le 1
$$
yielding the composite monad $T_{\mathrm{hom}} \coloneqq \overline{T}_{\mathrm{frag}} \circ \overline{T}_{\mathrm{pyr}}$ with multiplication $\mu_{\mathrm{hom}} = (\mu_f \overline{T}_p) \circ (\overline{T}_f \overline{T}_f \mu_p) \circ (\overline{T}_f \widehat{\lambda} \overline{T}_p)$.
:::
:::

## §2.6–2.7: Syntrix Stability ($\BoxSyn \phi$) & Spine Reflexivity ($\rho^{(n)}$) {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: HEREDITARY STABILITY &amp; GRADED REFLECTION (THM. 2.30)</div>

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
### Hereditary Semantics & Sequent Rules for $\BoxSyn$
Unlike $\Box_S \phi$ (horizontal aspect-relative necessity across $d_P(U,V) < \epsilon_A$), $\BoxSyn \phi$ measures **vertical ancestral grounding** down the Syntrix derivation tree to $\mathbf{AP}_0$:
$$
(U, k) \models \BoxSyn \phi \iff (U, k) \models \phi \;\wedge\; \forall X \in P_p\big((X, \phi) \in I_{p+1} \implies (U, k) \models \BoxSyn X\big)
$$

::: {.thm-box}
**Proof-Theoretic Sequent Rules for $\BoxSyn$ (§2.6.2):**
$$
\frac{a_i \in \mathbf{AP}_0 \quad S(x); \Gamma \vdash^0 a_i}{S(x); \Gamma \vdash^0 \BoxSyn a_i}\;(\BoxSyn\mathfrak{a}I), \qquad \frac{S(x); \Gamma \vdash^{j+1} \BoxSyn \phi' \quad ((X, \phi') \in I_{j+1})}{S(x); \Gamma \vdash^j \BoxSyn X}\;(\BoxSyn E_{\mathrm{IGP}})
$$
:::
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
::: {.carnap-box}
**Definition 2.29 & Theorem 2.30: Spine Reflexivity $\rho^{(n)}$**
On the thin spine subcategory $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{spine}} \hookrightarrow \mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{SL}}$, repeated structural lifting defines a natural transformation $\rho^{(n)} \colon \operatorname{Id}_{\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{spine}}} \Longrightarrow \Shift^n|_{\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{spine}}}$:
$$
\begin{matrix}
\mathbf{L}^{(k)} & \xrightarrow{\;\;\rho_k^{(n)} = \operatorname{Lift}_{\BoxSyn}^n\;\;} & \mathbf{L}^{(k+n)} \\
\downarrow\scriptstyle f_k & \circlearrowright & \downarrow\scriptstyle \Shift^n(f_k) \\
\mathbf{L}^{(k+1)} & \xrightarrow{\;\;\rho_{k+1}^{(n)} = \operatorname{Lift}_{\BoxSyn}^n\;\;} & \mathbf{L}^{(k+1+n)}
\end{matrix}
$$
satisfying the $(\mathbb{N}_0, +)$-graded reflection coherence law:
$$
\rho_{k+n}^{(m)} \circ \rho_k^{(n)} \;=\; \rho_k^{(n+m)}
$$
:::

## §2.8–2.11: The *Äondyne* Fibration, Quasi-Analysis & Synthesis {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-c">STRATUM A/B/C: GROTHENDIECK FIBRATION (THM. 2.32) &amp; CHAPTER 2 SYNTHESIS</div>

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.thm-box}
**Definition 2.31 & Theorem 2.32: The *Äondyne* Fibration**
A parameterized *Äondyne* over $U \in \Ctx$ is a tuple $\underline{\mathbf{S}} = (\metrophor, f, \vec{\gamma}, \gamma, \mathsf{Sel}_m)$ with smooth sections $\metrophor \in C^0(M_U, (P^U)^n)$ and $f \in C^0(M'_U, \Osyn(\vec{\gamma}; \gamma))$. The Grothendieck construction:
$$
\pi \colon \int_{\Ctx} \mathbf{Syn} \longrightarrow \Ctx, \qquad (U, \underline{\mathbf{S}}) \longmapsto U
$$
is a **Grothendieck fibration** whose Cartesian lifts transport entire Syntrix hierarchies across context manifolds, and whose closed loops (*Metrophorische Zirkel*, $L = \binom{Z}{2}$) act as holonomy selectors.
:::

::: {.carnap-box .fragment}
**Theorem 2.35: Carnapian Quasi-Analysis via Tree Monads**
Operationalizes Carnap's *Quasianalyse* (*Aufbau*, 1928) in $\Ban$:
$$
\operatorname{QuasiAnalyse}(X) \;\coloneqq\; T_{\mathsf{P}}(X) \in \operatorname{Alg}_{\Osyn}(\Ban)
$$
Higher concepts are coinvariant trees of operadic relations, not reified metaphysical substances (French 2014).
:::

<script>
function comb(n, k) {
  if (k < 0 || k > n) return 0;
  if (k === 0 || k === n) return 1;
  let res = 1;
  for (let i = 1; i <= k; i++) {
    res = res * (n - i + 1) / i;
  }
  return Math.round(res);
}

function fact(n) {
  let r = 1;
  for (let i = 2; i <= n; i++) r *= i;
  return r;
}

function setPermStab(mode) {
  const cTeal = "#20B2AA", cOrange = "#FFA500", cPurple = "#9370DB", cBlue = "#4169E1", cRed = "#DC143C", cGold = "#FFD700";
  let colors = [];
  let text = "";
  if (mode === 'sym') {
    colors = [cGold, cGold, cGold, cGold, cGold, cGold];
    text = "Stab(f) = Σ₃ (|Stab(f)| = 6)  ⇒  r_f = 6 / 6 = 1 Orbit (Fully Symmetric Operation)";
  } else if (mode === 's1') {
    colors = [cTeal, cTeal, cOrange, cPurple, cPurple, cOrange];
    text = "Stab(f) = ⟨s₁⟩ = {e, (12)} (|Stab(f)| = 2)  ⇒  r_f = 6 / 2 = 3 Coset Orbits (Fig. 2.2)";
  } else if (mode === 'a3') {
    colors = [cTeal, cOrange, cTeal, cOrange, cTeal, cOrange];
    text = "Stab(f) = A₃ (Cyclic Subgroup, |Stab(f)| = 3)  ⇒  r_f = 6 / 3 = 2 Chiral Coset Orbits";
  } else {
    colors = [cTeal, cOrange, cPurple, cBlue, cRed, cGold];
    text = "Stab(f) = {e} (|Stab(f)| = 1)  ⇒  r_f = 6 / 1 = 6 Distinct Orbits (Completely Asymmetric)";
  }
  for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) {
    document.getElementById('nd-' + i).setAttribute('fill', colors[i]);
  }
  document.getElementById('perm-readout').innerText = text;
}

function updateSelectionDims() {
  let n = parseInt(document.getElementById('sel-n').value);
  let m = parseInt(document.getElementById('sel-m').value);
  document.getElementById('sel-n-val').innerText = n;
  document.getElementById('sel-m-val').innerText = m;

  let s1 = comb(n, m);
  let s2 = (m <= n) ? s1 * fact(m) : 0;
  let s3 = comb(n + m - 1, m);
  let s4 = Math.pow(n, m);

  let html = `
    <div style="color:#4169E1;"><b>S₍₁₎ Het, Sym (Λ^m V):</b> C(${n}, ${m}) = <b style="color:#FFD700;">${s1.toLocaleString()}</b> ${s1 === 0 ? '<span style="color:#DC143C;">(Syndromabschluß!)</span>' : ''}</div>
    <div style="color:#20B2AA;"><b>S₍₂₎ Het, Asym (V^{⊗_distinct m}):</b> n!/(n-m)! = <b style="color:#FFD700;">${s2.toLocaleString()}</b></div>
    <div style="color:#FFA500;"><b>S₍₃₎ Hom, Sym (Sym^m V):</b> C(${n+m-1}, ${m}) = <b style="color:#FFD700;">${s3.toLocaleString()}</b></div>
    <div style="color:#9370DB;"><b>S₍₄₎ Hom, Asym (V^{⊗m}):</b> ${n}^${m} = <b style="color:#FFD700;">${s4.toLocaleString()}</b></div>
  `;
  document.getElementById('sel-bars').innerHTML = html;
}

function setSelPreset(n, m) {
  document.getElementById('sel-n').value = n;
  document.getElementById('sel-m').value = m;
  updateSelectionDims();
}

function updateTrichotomy() {
  let n0 = parseInt(document.getElementById('tri-n0').value);
  let m = parseInt(document.getElementById('tri-m').value);
  document.getElementById('tri-n0-val').innerText = n0;
  document.getElementById('tri-m-val').innerText = m;

  let seq = [n0];
  let curr = n0;
  for (let g = 1; g <= 5; g++) {
    if (curr > 10000) {
      seq.push("1.11 × 10¹⁴ (Diverges!)");
      break;
    }
    curr = comb(curr, m);
    seq.push(curr);
  }

  let regime = "";
  let color = "#FFD700";
  if (n0 <= m) {
    regime = "SUB-CRITICAL EXTINCTION (n₀ ≤ m ⇒ Syndromabschluß at γ ≤ 2)";
    color = "#ff6b81";
  } else if (n0 === m + 1) {
    regime = "CRITICAL EQUI-SYNDROMATIC FIXED POINT (n₀ = m + 1 ⇒ Constant Population)";
    color = "#20B2AA";
  } else {
    regime = "SUPER-CRITICAL DOUBLY-EXPONENTIAL REGIME (n₀ ≥ m + 2 ⇒ Rapid Explosion)";
    color = "#FFA500";
  }

  let box = document.getElementById('tri-trajectory');
  box.style.color = color;
  box.innerHTML = `<b>Regime:</b> ${regime}<br><b>Trajectory (γ = 0 … 5):</b> ` + seq.join("  →  ");
}

function setTriPreset(n0, m) {
  document.getElementById('tri-n0').value = n0;
  document.getElementById('tri-m').value = m;
  updateTrichotomy();
}

function showBeckLaw(step) {
  let box = document.getElementById('beck-display');
  if (step === 1) {
    box.innerHTML = `<b>[Prop. 2.28 Recursive Interchange Law]:</b><br>λ_X(ψ(u₁, …, u_n)) = [ μ_frag ∘ T̄_frag(ψ)(λ_X(u₁), …, λ_X(u_n)) ]_{I_exchange}<br>⇒ Pushes fragment operations outward across pyramidal node ψ modulo Boardman–Vogt exchange!`;
  } else if (step === 2) {
    box.innerHTML = `<b>[Fig. 2.7(A) Beck Multiplication Pentagon]:</b><br>μ_hom := (μ_frag T̄_pyr) ∘ (T̄_frag T̄_frag μ_pyr) ∘ (T̄_frag λ̂ T̄_pyr)<br>⇒ Guarantees that composite monad multiplication on T_hom = T̄_frag ∘ T̄_pyr is strictly associative!`;
  } else {
    box.innerHTML = `<b>[Fig. 2.7(B) Beck Unit Triangles]:</b><br>(1) λ ∘ T̄_pyr η_frag = η_frag T̄_pyr   and   (2) λ ∘ η_pyr T̄_frag = T̄_frag η_pyr<br>⇒Verified in Lean 4 (Syntrometrie.StratumA.Operads.BeckDistributiveLaw).`;
  }
}

document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function() {
  updateSelectionDims();
  updateTrichotomy();
});
</script>
